title: House Office of Legislative Counsel Modernization Act
official_summary:
House Office of Legislative Counsel Modernization Act

This act authorizes the designation of more than one attorney in the Office of the Legislative Counsel of the House of Representatives as Deputy Legislative Counsel. (Previously, the law authorized only one deputy.)

A Deputy Legislative Counsel must perform the functions of the Legislative Counsel during the Legislative Counsel's disability or absence (including a vacancy in the office).

summary.headline: New law lets the House legal drafting office name more than one Deputy Legislative Counsel instead of just one.
summary.what_it_does: The House Office of the Legislative Counsel is the office that helps House members write bills. Before this law, only one attorney in that office could be named Deputy Legislative Counsel. This law allows more than one attorney to hold that title. A deputy must carry out the head Legislative Counsel's duties when that person is absent, unable to serve, or the job is vacant.

who_it_affects.group: Attorneys in the House Office of the Legislative Counsel
who_it_affects.how: More than one of them can now be named Deputy Legislative Counsel and fill in for the head of the office when needed.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House of Representatives and their staff
who_it_affects.how: The office that drafts their bills can have several deputies to keep its work going when the head of the office is away or the job is empty.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 4, 2025; the summary does not give a separate start date.
